Open-source research software · official v0.1.1 release

From aquatic observations to reproducible movement science

Track, reconstruct, analyze and visualize aquatic-animal trajectories with R, Python and browser tools. Start with documented synthetic examples, then supply independent annotations, camera calibration and real recording metadata for scientific measurements.

Published software: AquaTrajectories v0.1.1 is a public GitHub release, permanently archived as 10.5281/zenodo.24262905 on Zenodo. CRAN qualification is in progress; this package is not yet published on CRAN.
Scientific status: this release is engineering-qualified, but biological identity, underwater metrology, fish welfare inference, empirical interval coverage and real actuator safety are not independently certified. See the evidence and limitations.

Discover the research workflows

Conceptual software workflow, not an empirical performance result.

01 · Acquire

Video tracking and identities

GoPro inputs, video PTS, YOLO/ByteTrack integration, tracker exports and manual annotation.

02 · Reconstruct

Multiview 3D and refraction

Stereo rigs, clock diagnostics, Brown correction, air–glass–water optics and geometric correspondence.

03 · Validate

Scientific benchmarks

Detection F1, IDF1, holdout targets, physical XYZ error and source-truth provenance.

04 · Characterize

Movement and schooling

Speed, paths, spatial occupancy, school geometry, 3D scenes and trajectory recurrence.

05 · Model

Behaviour and longitudinal models

Changepoints, Gaussian HMMs, FPCA, functional curves and nested tank/fish models.

06 · Question

Uncertainty-aware inference

Pixel, optical, identity and trajectory perturbations, with explicit model assumptions.

07 · Experiment

Events and independent tanks

Event alignment, tank-replicated summaries and defensible inferential units.

08 · Interact

Animal–Computer Interaction

Telemetry, choices, access inequality and bounded device-control research protocols.

09 · Communicate

All 22 plotting functions

Demonstration figures, publication storyboards, 3D projections and reproducible graphics.

A visual laboratory

Original scientific illustration. The geometry is schematic, not a measurement from a real tank.

Reproducible first steps 

# Install the official versioned GitHub release (not yet on CRAN)
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories", ref = "v0.1.1")

library(aquaTrajectories)
x <- aqt_simulate_tracks(n_fish = 5, n_frames = 200)
aqt_plot_paths(x)
kin <- aqt_kinematics(x, max_gap_s = 0.1)

This simulator produces synthetic random walks, not biologically calibrated fish movement.

Interactive synthetic trajectory explorer

Explore five invented trajectories in 3D, top, side and front projections. New learning controls demonstrate camera-local occlusion and ID switching: the synthetic positions remain the same while the apparent labels can change. This is a browser-only teaching illustration, not a real synchronized multiview recording or a validated tracking benchmark.

Open interactive synthetic explorerUnderstand occlusions and track IDs

Transparent evidence and reproducible figures

Before interpreting biological results, consult the capability and validation matrix, the research evidence dashboard, and the experiment design starter kit. The dashboard links to reproducible tests and original source-evidence contracts; it does not invent benchmark accuracies.

Explore all 22 plotting functions

The new complete plotting-function visual atlas documents all 22 aqt_plot_* exports: 16 actual base-R plotting outputs reproduced from openly labeled synthetic inputs, and six separately labeled projected input previews for optional interactive rgl plots. Search by function name or scientific category, inspect scientific limitations, and copy the runnable calls. No projected preview is presented as a captured native rgl scene.

Five complete, runnable publication figures

The five-figure reproducible workbook exercises actual native plotting functions with openly labeled synthetic data for feeding phases, physical XYZ error illustrations, replicated-tank occupancy, event-aligned speed, and heading roses. All five plots include source code and retain their scientific interpretation limits.
